beats.label: S1 · The Pact
beats.text: Bulldogs lose again and Nat nearly folds the team; Shoresy promises to never lose another game, with Sanguinet installed as player-coach.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the founding promise the whole series hangs on and the coaching structure for the season.

beats.label: S1 · The Recruits
beats.text: Shoresy recruits four washed-up veterans — Dolo, Goody, Hitch and JJ — plus three prison-guard Jims to serve as enforcers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces every player who will define the roster for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Blueberry Bulldogs
beats.text: Nat sells naming rights to the Blueberry Festival; the rebranded Bulldogs win their opener over Timmins on a JJ goal and constant Jim fights.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First win under the pact, and the festival money is the funding line that keeps the team alive.

beats.label: S1 · Michaels Returns
beats.text: Sacked coach Michaels agrees to return as goalie after Shoresy delivers a forced apology and Sanguinet cops to stealing his girlfriend.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts the season's last missing piece — goaltender — in place and resolves the pilot's grudge.

beats.label: S1 · The Brawl
beats.text: A hallway brawl with the North Bay Norsemen goes viral; the NOSHO tribunal awards Sudbury the forfeit and warns Nat to control her players.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Cements the Bulldogs' outlaw identity and shows the tribunal as a recurring gatekeeper.

beats.label: S1 · Chasing Laura
beats.text: Shoresy keeps trying to court local reporter Laura Mohr, who refuses to cover the Bulldogs — or him — until they actually matter.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Plants the season's romantic through-line that will run for years.

beats.label: S1 · Sold-Out Loss
beats.text: The Bulldogs lose their final regular-season game to the Soo but sell out the arena; Nat waives her ultimatum and sends them into the playoffs.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The team survives the fold-threat and enters the playoffs, launching next season's championship setup.

cliffhanger.text: The rebuilt Blueberry Bulldogs have gone from doormats to a packed-house team, and Nat has waived her fold-them-if-they-lose ultimatum. They head into the NOSHO playoffs against the Soo still owing Shoresy's promise to never lose.
questions: Can the Bulldogs get past the Soo Cyclones in the playoffs and cash Shoresy's promise?
Will the Laura Mohr thread ever go anywhere?
Can this brawling, resentful roster actually hold together off the ice?

characters.name: Shoresy
characters.line: Sudbury's foul-mouthed captain and the dirtiest player in hockey; has sworn to Nat he'll never lose another game.

characters.name: Nat
characters.line: Bulldogs owner; hired Sanguinet as player-coach and will fold the team the moment Shoresy breaks that promise.

characters.name: Sanguinet
characters.line: New player-coach; the reason Michaels was originally fired, having slept with Michaels' girlfriend.

characters.name: Michaels
characters.line: Fired as coach in the pilot, rehired as the Bulldogs' goalie after Shoresy delivered a grudging apology.

characters.name: Laura Mohr
characters.line: Local journalist Shoresy is trying to court; refuses to cover the Bulldogs — or him — until they're relevant.

characters.name: JJ Franky JJ
characters.line: Quebec star Shoresy once injured with a dirty hit; the team's top scorer, sleeps with actresses.

characters.name: Dolo
characters.line: Quebec rapper-turned-Bulldog whose pro career ended fighting a racist fan; his brawl videos went viral in Sudbury.

characters.name: Goody
characters.line: Brant 'Goody' Goodleaf, a Six Nations player who left hockey for pro lacrosse before Shoresy pulled him back.

characters.name: Hitch
characters.line: Ted 'Hitch' Hitchcock, a Newfoundland-born former 1st-round NHL pick coaxed out of retirement by Shoresy.

characters.name: The Jims
characters.line: Three Indigenous prison guards, all named Jim; the Bulldogs' enforcers, win most fights they start.

beats.label: S2 · The Streak
beats.text: Bulldogs come off the NOSHO title chasing an undefeated season; Shoresy's constant pressure — ice-cream slaps included — starts to grate on the room.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's stakes and the tension between Shoresy's discipline and the team's tolerance.

beats.label: S2 · Hunt Debut
beats.text: New American expansion team the Soo Hunt joins the league; Sudbury's stars let off-ice lives distract them from the streak.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the rival that will define next season's tournament and this season's road climax.

beats.label: S2 · Calendar Season
beats.text: JJ's solo calendar goes viral with Sudbury's Bear community; his Quebec exes call him out on TV, while Nat launches a team calendar to fund the tournament.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The calendars are the funding mechanism for hosting the National Senior Tournament — the payoff arc.

beats.label: S2 · Players Only
beats.text: Sanguinet calls a players-only meeting to reset focus; Michaels joins the Jims for their prison quiz and drills 'set the tone' into them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The internal reset that keeps the streak intact and further binds Michaels to the enforcer group.

beats.label: S2 · Tribunal Reprieve
beats.text: Shoresy fights his brawl suspension at the NOSHO tribunal and gets it overturned — the undefeated run survives into the American road trip.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Removes the season's biggest structural threat to the streak and keeps Shoresy on the ice for the finale.

beats.label: S2 · Laura Says Yes
beats.text: After a full season of rebuffs, Laura Mohr finally dances with Shoresy at a gay night; he later sleeps with her, and the flirtation becomes real.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The romantic thread from S1 finally lands; recurring from here.

beats.label: S2 · Sudbury Wins
beats.text: Bulldogs beat the Hunt on the road to stay unbeaten; calendar sales close the funding gap to host next season's National Senior Tournament in Sudbury.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Delivers both the undefeated season and the tournament host status that IS the S3 premise.

cliffhanger.text: The Bulldogs have finished the regular season undefeated and secured Sudbury as host of the National Senior Tournament. The NOSHO playoffs against the Hunt are next, and Shoresy is finally in something with Laura.
questions: Can Sudbury beat the Hunt when it counts most?
Will Shoresy's punishing pace on his own body catch up with him?
Now that Laura is actually with him, can he keep it together?

characters.name: Shoresy
characters.line: Captain driving the undefeated pursuit; his slap-the-ice-cream pressure is starting to grate on the room.

characters.name: Nat
characters.line: Owner; monetised the champion team via calendars to fund the coming National Senior Tournament in Sudbury.

characters.name: Sanguinet
characters.line: Player-coach who called the players-only reset when the team's focus slipped.

characters.name: Michaels
characters.line: Goalie; the season's most praised player, also helped the Jims win their prison quiz.

characters.name: Laura Mohr
characters.line: Sudbury reporter who finally lets Shoresy in — dancing with him, then sleeping with him.

characters.name: JJ Franky JJ
characters.line: Top scorer whose solo calendar sold out and whose Quebec exes publicly humiliated him on TV.

characters.name: Dolo, Goody & Hitch
characters.line: The three other veteran recruits; each spent this season more focused on relationships than the streak.

characters.name: The Jims
characters.line: Enforcers; distracted much of the year by their prison quiz tournament after their fourth member was stabbed.

beats.label: S3 · Title Lost
beats.text: Sudbury lose the NOSHO final to the Soo Hunt with Shoresy playing concussed; the city still hosts the National Senior Tournament as planned.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends the undefeated era, seeds Shoresy's head issues, and stages the tournament.

beats.label: S3 · Group Play
beats.text: The Bulldogs win their openers over Charlottetown and Vaughan; Canadesi enforcer Sly Sylvestri slashes Shoresy's ankle, stacking a leg injury onto the head.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the tournament format, introduces Gord's team, and compounds Shoresy's physical decline.

beats.label: S3 · Barrelmen Hit
beats.text: Shoresy overrules Sanguinet and takes the ice himself against Brooks' enforcers; a huge hit gives him a second concussion in weeks.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The injury that forces the retirement conversation and drives every subsequent decision this season.

beats.label: S3 · Ruled Out
beats.text: Nat rules Shoresy out of the Hunt semi-final and tells him he needs to look at retirement — the team needs protecting from him, not by him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First moment Shoresy is told his playing career is done; sets up his post-hockey question.

beats.label: S3 · Fans in the Stands
beats.text: 3-0 down in the semi, Shoresy contributes the only way left to him and starts a brawl with Hunt fans in the stands; a final suspension looms.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows how far Shoresy will go to matter when he can't play, and threatens his final appearance.

beats.label: S3 · Final Speech
beats.text: Nat argues Shoresy back into the Rawdon final by pitching it as his last game; his speech drives a 5-4 comeback that wins the National title.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The playing-career farewell and the title that secures the offseason built around it.

beats.label: S3 · Two Offers
beats.text: Post-tournament, Shoresy weighs a BroDude analyst job against Nat's pitch to hang up the skates and coach the Bulldogs instead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The choice that is the entire spine of the following season.

cliffhanger.text: The Bulldogs are National champions but Shoresy has to retire after two concussions. A BroDude analyst gig and Nat's coaching offer both sit on the table, and Laura is finally in reach.
questions: Will Shoresy take the BroDude job, coach the Bulldogs, or neither?
What does a Bulldogs offseason without Shoresy on the ice actually look like?
Now that Laura is warming up, can Shoresy build a life with her?

characters.name: Shoresy
characters.line: Concussed twice this year and told he's done playing; still delivered the National-title speech.

characters.name: Nat
characters.line: Owner who publicly saved Shoresy for the final while privately telling him to retire and coach instead.

characters.name: Sanguinet
characters.line: Coach; refused to send in the Jims against the Barrelmen, which drove Shoresy onto the ice and into the hit.

characters.name: Michaels
characters.line: Goalie; helped backstop the tournament run.

characters.name: Laura Mohr
characters.line: Girlfriend-adjacent; interviewed Shoresy pre-final with real chemistry for the first time.

characters.name: JJ Franky JJ
characters.line: Top scorer distracted trying to win back ex-fiancée Marie-Mai, who owns the Quebec finalists.

characters.name: Dolo, Goody & Hitch
characters.line: The three other veteran recruits; carried much of the tournament run while Shoresy was hurt.

characters.name: The Jims
characters.line: Enforcers; used to punish the Canadesi's dirty play in the group stage.

characters.name: Gord Gallant
characters.line: 'Gorgeous' Gord, captain of the Charlottetown Reds and the tournament's charm-offensive rival.

beats.label: S4 · Summer Empty
beats.text: Most Bulldogs scatter for the summer, but Shoresy, Dolo, Hitch, Goody and Michaels stay in Sudbury; Shoresy takes a BroDude webshow gig and feels empty.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The core offseason setup: Shoresy trying life after hockey, refusing to coach.

beats.label: S4 · Sean Avery
beats.text: Shoresy tanks his own show — respect for Gilmour and McSorley makes him too polite — so producers add Sean Avery as a third host to spark him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shows why the BroDude path can't be Shoresy's answer; the format won't hold him.

beats.label: S4 · The Juniors
beats.text: In exchange for Weird Sudbury invites, the Bulldogs mentor four juniors heading to the OHL: Caleb, Carter, Jack and Mason.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Jack, whose thread continues, and the mentoring dynamic that ends up defining Shoresy's decision.

beats.label: S4 · Proving It
beats.text: Shoresy chases Laura Mohr all summer — gardening her house, karaoke Alanis, refusing other advances — under her 'you have to be sure' rule.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The relationship pivot from flirtation to commitment; drives the finale.

beats.label: S4 · Kangaroo Court
beats.text: The Jims sleep with the veterans' casual partners after being 'big-timed'; a kangaroo court hosted by Michaels resets the room.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The internal conflict of the season; ends with the roster back on the same page for the coaching handover.

beats.label: S4 · The Marathon
beats.text: Shoresy runs the marathon Laura once told him to and forgot; she takes him in, and he tells Nat he'll coach the Bulldogs next season.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The two decisions that end the offseason — being with Laura, taking the coaching job — both happen here.

beats.label: S4 · Skip the Party
beats.text: The team skip Weird Sudbury to back Jack in his festival dance for Maria; the offseason ends with the Bulldogs bought into the juniors and into coaching.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Confirms the emotional handoff; the group has picked the juniors over the party they spent the season chasing.

cliffhanger.text: Shoresy has accepted the Bulldogs' coaching job, Laura has finally let him in, and the veteran roster is invested in the next generation. The season ahead starts with him behind the bench for the first time.
questions: What does a Shoresy-coached Bulldogs season actually look like?
Can Shoresy and Laura hold this together once real life is on the table?
Do the juniors — especially Jack — stay in the picture?

characters.name: Shoresy
characters.line: Retired player; agreed at the end of summer to coach the Bulldogs next season, and finally in it with Laura.

characters.name: Nat
characters.line: Owner; convinced Shoresy to coach by telling him how she chose to love hockey after her mother died.

characters.name: Laura Mohr
characters.line: Shoresy's partner after a summer of him proving he's sure — gardening, karaoke Alanis, a marathon on her say-so.

characters.name: Dolo, Hitch & Goody
characters.line: The summer holdouts; slept with the juniors' moms and got dragged through the kangaroo court.

characters.name: Michaels
characters.line: Fellow summer holdout; presided over the kangaroo court that reset the room.

characters.name: The Jims
characters.line: Slept with the vets' casual partners for being 'big-timed'; ordered to make amends and did.

characters.name: Jack
characters.line: The most invested of the four juniors; serenaded Maria at karaoke and led the festival dance.

beats.label: S5 · North Bay Visit
beats.text: Shoresy visits Jack in North Bay Juniors and pulls him out of a slump; billet mother Jill propositions Shoresy, who declines out of loyalty to Laura.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Confirms Shoresy's mentor role and his commitment to Laura before the season's stakes hit.

beats.label: S5 · League Folds
beats.text: On Shoresy's first day as coach the NOSHO folds — only the Bulldogs and Hunt survive — and the city hands their locker room to a basketball team.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The premise-breaking event: the league Shoresy built the team in no longer exists.

beats.label: S5 · The Challenge
beats.text: On BroDude, Shoresy rants that physical Canadian hockey is dying; Gretzky calls to praise him and touring European coach Teppo Maki takes it as a challenge.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kicks off the season-defining EU showdown and gives the show a rival head coach.

beats.label: S5 · The Northstars
beats.text: Shoresy assembles the NOSHO Northstars from tournament all-stars, brings his brother Morris in as assistant, and drills a winning culture from day one.
beats.whyLoadBearing: New team, new coaching staff, new stakes — the vehicle for everything that follows.

beats.label: S5 · Forgotten
beats.text: A 6am warm-up draws no fans and breaks Shoresy; Nat books an outdoor rink for the EU game after Sudbury cheers the Bulldogs at a basketball game.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The venue for the finale and Shoresy's grief about being forgotten, both resolved here.

beats.label: S5 · Total Buy-In
beats.text: Laura is game for a threesome with Jill but Shoresy passes; the Northstars clear every personal beef before puck drop to secure total buy-in.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shoresy's own line-drawing and the team's alignment; both feed the win.

beats.label: S5 · Outdoor Comeback
beats.text: The Northstars come back from 3-0 down to beat the EU 4-3 in a bench-clearing outdoor game; Shoresy moves in with Laura afterward.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The signature win and the personal step forward — the season's two payoffs together.

cliffhanger.text: The NOSHO is dead but the Northstars beat the touring Europeans on an outdoor rink in Sudbury, and Shoresy is now coach, cohabitant with Laura, and something close to family with her son Ben. The league he built the team in no longer exists.
questions: Where do the Bulldogs actually play now that the NOSHO has folded?
Can Shoresy make domestic life work in Sudbury with no ice to bleed off on?
What does the relationship with Teppo and the Europeans become from here?

characters.name: Shoresy
characters.line: Bulldogs coach and NOSHO Northstars head coach; now cohabiting with Laura in Sudbury.

characters.name: Nat
characters.line: Owner who conjured the Northstars roster and the outdoor rink venue when the NOSHO collapsed under her.

characters.name: Laura Mohr
characters.line: Shoresy's partner and now cohabitant; encouraged him to consider a threesome he ultimately declined.

characters.name: Morris
characters.line: Shoresy's brother, pulled in as assistant coach; a rare source of emotional vulnerability for Shoresy.

characters.name: Teppo Maki
characters.line: Head coach of the touring European team; began as antagonist, ended as friend and sparring partner.

characters.name: Jack
characters.line: Now a junior in North Bay; Shoresy's protégé, playing better after his coach visit.

characters.name: The veteran Bulldogs
characters.line: Dolo, Goody, Hitch, JJ, Michaels and the Jims — now the senior figures on the Northstars roster.
